patch.value: Official Home Assistant 2026.7 documentation specifies supported_features with coalesce_messages as the first post-auth command and an admin-only subscribe_trigger contract accepting one or more automation triggers plus optional variables. Current Core dev source validates trigger configs, emits event messages containing variables/context, and uses unsubscribe_events for cleanup. The live configured Core accepts both contracts. The CLI currently supports only subscribe_events and assumes every incoming frame is one JSON object.

Implement the latest stable Home Assistant WebSocket supported-features negotiation and typed subscribe_trigger workflow so agents can observe automation triggers with bounded, token-efficient output.

The client negotiates coalesce_messages as command id 1 immediately after authentication and correctly dispatches both single-object and coalesced-array frames; hassio ws subscribe-trigger accepts inline JSON or a JSON file, optional variables, bounded wait/max-event controls, and provides detailed examples and global help; Trigger subscriptions validate input before network I/O, unsubscribe reliably, preserve generic passthrough, and remain read-only safe; All source coverage remains 100/100/100/100, docstrings remain complete, every source file stays within 300 code lines, and all formatter/help/schema/live/release/security/PM gates pass
Official docs and current Core source agree; live read-only negotiation and trigger subscription succeed; all-status PM search finds no duplicate
Let agents observe meaningful automation conditions instead of consuming the entire event bus.
Reduces framing and token overhead while adding a stable typed streaming primitive.
A production-ready typed trigger subscription surface with coalesced protocol handling and exact-head delivery proof.
The stable latest API documents subscribe_trigger and coalescing, but the existing CLI cannot use the former or decode the latter.
